FISA statute enacted, authorizing FISA Court orders for electronic surveillance and searches of foreign powers or their agents.
Fourth Circuit decides United States v. Truong Dinh Hung, establishing the 'primary purpose' standard for foreign intelligence surveillance.
CIA employee Aldrich Ames arrested on espionage charges; the FBI investigation involved multiple FISA certifications.
Scruggs proposed amending the Attorney General's FCI Guidelines so that criminal-conduct questions in intelligence investigations would be raised first with OIPR.
actors: Office of Intelligence Policy and Review

events.description: New York FBI learned Hazmi and Mihdhar were in the United States; the wall barred criminal investigators from the search.
Donna e-mails John that Chad will open an intelligence case and that there is a more definitive Mihdhar connection to the Cole attack.
Donna requests, through the NSA representative to the FBI, permission to pass NSA information associating Mihdhar with a suspected terrorist facility to Cole investigators.
Donna sends Chad a draft EC requesting an intelligence investigation to locate Mihdhar, marked 'routine' precedence.
Jason forwards the EC at about 2:00 p.m. to Bin Laden squad agents including Scott and directs Jay to open an intelligence investigation and assign it to Richard.
Conference call among Scott, Donna and Rob on whether to open a criminal or intelligence investigation of Mihdhar; Scott had been asked to delete the EC.
Donna and Rob consult NSLU attorney Susan, who reportedly supports opening an intelligence investigation and excluding a criminal agent from any Mihdhar interview.
Donna e-mails Jason and Scott conveying the NSLU opinion; Scott replies that someday someone will die because of the wall; Donna replies that FBIHQ is also frustrated.
Information on the Khallad identification in the Kuala Lumpur photographs is officially passed to the FBI in a CIR.
Mihdhar travels to the United States (as outlined in the EC).
Mihdhar and Hazmi travel to the United States.
FBI San Diego opened a preliminary inquiry on Bayoumi.
Bayoumi preliminary inquiry closed without conversion to full investigation.
Bayoumi and Dyson met Hazmi and Mihdhar at a halal restaurant in Los Angeles.
Hazmi and Mihdhar traveled to San Diego within days of the meeting and rented an apartment arranged by Bayoumi.
Long-distance call from the Hazmi/Mihdhar apartment to al Qaeda-linked facility in the Middle East.
Bayoumi obtained a US visa in Jeddah; returned to US May 31, 2000.
Hazmi and Mihdhar moved into the home of the FBI San Diego asset as boarders.
Mihdhar left the United States.
The asset was opened as an FBI asset, recruited by Stan.
Bayoumi left the United States permanently; was in England on 9/11.
John accessed the March 2000 CIA cable stating Mihdhar, Hazmi and another person traveled from Malaysia to Bangkok on January 8, 2000, and Hazmi flew to Los Angeles.
Mihdhar, Hazmi and another person traveled from Malaysia to Bangkok.
Hazmi left Bangkok for Hong Kong then Los Angeles.
Quso traveled to Bangkok to deliver $7,000 to Khallad.
Peter completed CTC report finding UBL/al Qaeda circumstantially tied to the Cole attack.
John sent a mid-May e-mail to Peter noting Mihdhar's travel and courier links.
Peter replied by e-mail asking whether anyone had mapped the East Asia travel.
John obtained three Kuala Lumpur surveillance photographs from CIA records.
ITOS IA accessed Phoenix EC in ACS and assigned lead to Ellen in the RFU.
RFU IA delivered hard copy of Phoenix EC to Jane in the UBLU.
Jane downloaded Phoenix EC; Ellen closed the RFU lead noting UBLU would research, no action at the time.
SSA Chris left FBI Headquarters.
Robin printed the Phoenix EC from ACS while researching Ibn Khattab for the Moussaoui FISA request; she did not share it.
Martin and Robin consulted NSLU attorney Tim about the Moussaoui FISA case; Tim advised insufficient evidence of a foreign power.
September 11 attacks, discussed in the Moussaoui chapter outline.
Information about Moussaoui received from British authorities on September 12 and 13.
Moussaoui's arrest by the Minneapolis FBI, followed by a hotel room search and Al-Attas interview and arrest.
Moussaoui's indictment.
events.place: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia

events.description: Plot in Jordan to disrupt New Year activities with explosives uncovered and thwarted; 16 arrested.
Ahmad Ressam stopped at US/Canadian border in Washington state with a vehicle loaded with explosives.
Hazmi (and Mihdhar) boarded United Airlines flight from Bangkok to Los Angeles.
NSA information on planned Kuala Lumpur travel appeared in the daily threat update to the FBI Director.
Mihdhar arrived in Kuala Lumpur on a Saudi passport with valid U.S. visa; passport photocopied and sent to CIA HQ.
Dwight began drafting a CIR to pass Mihdhar's visa information to FBI around 9:30 a.m.; Michelle added a hold note around 4:00 p.m.
By mid-February the CIR had still not been sent to the FBI; Dwight asked a contractor to save the draft CIR.
Martin and Gary discuss FISA options for Moussaoui; Martin says it is not an emergency and lacks foreign power link.
Minneapolis FBI seeks CIA and London Legat help to link Moussaoui to al Qaeda; Henry e-mails Craig with Al-Attas address book data.
Bombing of the U.S.S. Cole in Yemen, referenced by Martin regarding past ease of FISA approvals.
Martin, Robin, and FAA employee meet Don at RFU to decide what to tell FAA about Moussaoui.
CTC employee James briefed FBI SSA Bob at SIOC about Mihdhar's travel to Malaysia; no mention of U.S. visa.
James briefed FBI SSA Ted on the second Malaysia meetings cable; Ted sent update to ITOS Assistant Section Chief at 8:40 a.m.
CIA cables reported a new individual joined Mihdhar and that Mihdhar and Hazmi departed Kuala Lumpur for Bangkok; both arrived in Bangkok January 8.
CIA Bin Laden Unit prepared a cable asking that Mihdhar and associates be identified in Thailand.
Hazmi and Mihdhar flew from Bangkok to Los Angeles, admitted on non-immigrant visas.
Bangkok officials reported internally identifying Hazmi and his travel to Los Angeles; not shared with FBI until August 2001.
The Patriot Act changed FISA requirement from 'the purpose' to 'a significant purpose,' permitting consultation between intelligence and criminal investigators.
David Kris testified before Congress on the need for intelligence and law enforcement to work together.

Henry consulted RFU Unit Chief Don about opening a criminal case against Moussaoui; Don said probable cause was shaky and suggested consulting the CDC; Henry wrote 'Not opened per instructions of [Unit Chief Don]'.
May 2003 bombings in Saudi Arabia and Morocco. FBI personnel and experts were deployed to assist the investigations.
Minneapolis FBI (Gary, Henry) explores placing an undercover Arabic-speaking officer in Moussaoui's jail cell; Don at HQ tells them not to proceed.
Translation of Al-Attas' will and taped call with imam Ahmed forwarded by Roy to Don.
Paris ALAT provides additional French information on Moussaoui, including statements from Idir.
Martin telephones Gary relaying French interest in having Moussaoui escorted to France.
Chicago FBI linguist completes translation of Al-Attas' will and tape; Henry forwards to FBIHQ.
George Tenet named Director of Central Intelligence.
FBI began detailing employees to the CIA's Counterterrorist Center.
Eric detailed to CTC as branch chief for a terrorist group.
Eric transferred to deputy chief of the Bin Laden Unit.
Eric left the Bin Laden Unit.
Craig replaced Eric as FBI deputy chief detailee.
Mary assigned to CIA HQ from FBI WFO.
Nearly simultaneous vehicle bombs at U.S. embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam killed over 200 and injured over 4,000.
events.place: Nairobi, Kenya; Dar es Salaam, Tanzania

events.description: Early January debriefing of joint FBI/CIA source, who identified Khallad in Kuala Lumpur photographs; CIA did not inform FBI.
FBI Headquarters and CIA discussed status of information on the Cole attack and Khallad in May and June 2001.
Scott became a special agent in the FBI's New York Office after Navy service.
Scott assigned to TWA Flight 800 investigation.
Scott transferred to the Bin Laden squad after East African embassy bombings.
actors: FBI New York Field Office Bin Laden Squad

events.description: Bin Laden indicted in the Southern District of New York.
Donna assigned to work on the Cole investigation.
Criminal search warrant granted for Moussaoui's belongings, executed at INS offices in Minnesota.
FBI ALAT in London contacted British authorities requesting traces on Moussaoui.
ALAT gave British French-provided information about Moussaoui.
London Legat again requested Moussaoui information from the British.
Moussaoui indicted by a grand jury on six conspiracy counts related to the September 11 attacks.
Al-Attas pled guilty to making false statements.
Al-Attas sentenced to time served.
Baker became Counsel of OIPR.
Robin accessed and printed the Phoenix EC after searching ACS for 'Ibn Khattab' but did not share it.
FBI Headquarters disseminated a teletype to the Intelligence Community about Moussaoui without Minneapolis's threat assessment.
Martin edited the Minneapolis FISA request, deleting three paragraphs on Moussaoui's connections to Khattab; Gary objected.
Henry wrote a memorandum assessing the threat Moussaoui posed, for the FAA, as deportation to France with sky marshals was considered.

The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court of Review issued an opinion allowing intelligence information, including FISA-derived information, to be shared between intelligence and criminal investigators (text is badly garbled).
actors: Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court of Review

events.description: The Attorney General, Secretary of Homeland Security and Director of Central Intelligence signed an MOU on sharing, handling and use of information related to terrorist threats and vulnerabilities (the month is garbled in the OCR).
Bombings in Saudi Arabia and Morocco, to which the FBI deployed personnel and experts to help investigate.
Craig e-mails Don that CIA had not received formal FBI communication on Moussaoui.
Don asks Martin and Robin to prepare a comprehensive teletype to the CIA; recommends FAA sky marshals to Roy.
Martin's 11-page teletype on Moussaoui issued to multiple agencies; Gary told not to give the LHM to the FAA.
Henry meets the INS supervisor on Moussaoui's deportation, e-mails Martin; later Henry and an INS agent brief the Minneapolis FAA office.
Don questions the expense of a JPATS flight and advocates FAA sky marshals.
Don informs Roy that FBI HQ concurs with a Minneapolis agent accompanying Moussaoui to France.
Mihdhar entered the United States and had not departed.
Hazmi traveled to the United States.
John emailed Bin Laden Unit managers about threats in Malaysia and possible links to the Malaysia meetings.
John emailed CTC managers about the source's identification of Khallad and recommended sending it to the FBI via CIR.
Donna and Mary exchanged emails on Kuala Lumpur photographs, Mihdhar's flight manifest and access to Quso; a meeting was tentatively set for Aug 15 but apparently did not occur.
Mary found cables on Hazmi's travel and learned Mihdhar had entered the US on July 4, 2001.
FBI began an investigation to locate Mihdhar without great urgency; NY criminal agents were excluded.
CIA provided Khallad identification information to the FBI.
Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act signed into law, establishing the FTO designation process.
The first 30 FTO designations were made by the Secretary of State.
37 FTOs on the State Department list, including al Qaeda, Ansar al-Islam and FARC.
At the time of the Moussaoui investigation, FBI HQ SSAs were responsible for ensuring FISA requests were supported before presentation to OIPR.
actors: Office of Intelligence Policy and Review

events.description: At the Department's direction, the FBI established special wall procedures for the New York Field Office's criminal and intelligence investigations arising from the 1993 WTC bombing.
OIPR began including wall procedure descriptions in all FISA applications filed with the FISA Court when a criminal investigation was open.
actors: Office of Intelligence Policy and Review

events.description: Attorney General Reno directed termination of certain FISA surveillances over concerns about primary purpose.
In late 1999 the Department proposed using the FISA Court as 'the wall' for Millennium threat applications.
OIG issued its Campaign Finance Report on handling of FBI intelligence information.
actors: Office of the Inspector General, Department of Justice

events.description: AGRT made interim recommendations to the Attorney General, including regular briefings to the Criminal Division.
Attorney General Reno established the Core Group for monthly critical case briefings.
AGRT issued its final report (Bellows report) on the Wen Ho Lee investigation.
GAO issued a report discussing the 1995 Procedures and the wall.
The September 11 terrorist attacks are cited as prompting FBI reforms in counterterrorism operations and analysis.
The Director approved the FBI's Human Talent for Intelligence Production Concept of Operations (CONOPS) for recruiting and training intelligence analysts.
The FBI placed an intelligence analyst recruitment advertisement in the Washington Post, Washington Times and New York Times.
The FBI National Press Office issued the first press release on intelligence analyst recruitment.
The second press release was issued, featuring an interview with EAD for Intelligence Maureen A. Baginski and two analysts.

OIG completed its report on the FBI's handling of intelligence information related to the September 11 attacks. It was classified Top Secret/SCI and provided to the FBI, DOJ, Congress, CIA, NSA and the 9/11 Commission.
actors: Office of the Inspector General, Department of Justice
National Commission on Terrorist Attacks Upon the United States

events.description: The Court allowed the OIG to release sections of the unclassified report that did not discuss Moussaoui.
actors: Office of the Inspector General, Department of Justice
United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia

events.description: The Moussaoui case concluded when the Court sentenced Zacarias Moussaoui to life in prison.
actors: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia

events.description: OIG released the full unclassified version of the report, including the Moussaoui chapter.
actors: Office of the Inspector General, Department of Justice

events.description: Deputy Attorney General Thompson issued a memorandum on the wall between intelligence and criminal terrorism investigations.
Hazmi and Mihdhar entered the United States.
Hazmi and Mihdhar met Omar al-Bayoumi in Los Angeles about two weeks after entering the US.
Hazmi and Mihdhar moved to San Diego, where Bayoumi helped them get an apartment; they stayed four months.
San Diego FBI closed its preliminary inquiry on Bayoumi.
Bayoumi's name first surfaced at the FBI in connection with other investigations.
FBI Headquarters established counterterrorism as a top FBI priority.
Yemenis provide FBI with photograph of Khallad and other Cole suspects.
CIA officer debriefs source with Max present; source identifies Khallad in Yemeni-provided photo.
Quso travels to Bangkok with $7,000 from Ibrahim to deliver to Khallad.
Mihdhar, Hazmi and another individual leave Malaysia and travel to Bangkok.
CIA cables link Khallad theory to Mihdhar; CTC forwards Kuala Lumpur photo of Mihdhar to show source.
CIA case officer debriefs source, who identifies Khallad in Kuala Lumpur Photo No. 1 (actually Hazmi) but cannot identify Mihdhar in Photo No. 2.
RFU IOS Robin accessed and printed the Phoenix EC after searching ACS for 'Ibn Khattab'; did not share it.
Meeting between RFU and NSLU chief Bowman assessing sufficiency of evidence for Moussaoui FISA; Bowman advised no agency link shown.

After 9/11 the FBI restructured the National Security Law Branch into three operational units. Two Counterterrorism Law Units handle counterterrorism and one Counterintelligence Law Unit handles counterintelligence and cyber. A fourth unit was recently added for policy and training.
The CIA watchlisted Khalid al-Mihdhar around the time of the millennium threat. The OCR is highly garbled, so this is uncertain.
INS arrested Moussaoui; Gary called USAO's Wesley about a criminal search warrant.
Second interview of Al-Attas at the INS District Office; Al-Attas arrested by INS for visa violation.
Henry and agents interviewed Moussaoui a second time; he requested an immigration lawyer and questioning ended.
Henry's 26-page EC uploaded into ACS; Henry returned Megan's call.
Donna e-mail setting out purpose of meeting with New York on the Cole investigation, focused on Nashiri.
Meeting at FBI New York Field Office between FBI HQ, CIA/CTC and New York Cole agents and AUSA Kelley; Donna showed Kuala Lumpur photographs and argument over 'the wall' ensued.
A New York agent tentatively identified one pictured individual in the Kuala Lumpur photographs as Quso but could not make a definitive identification.
Kuala Lumpur surveillance photographs taken in Malaysia around the Millennium.
CIA case officer debriefed the source, who identified Khallad in the Yemeni-provided photograph; ALAT heard it.
Cole case agent e-mailed Max requesting all the source knows about Khallad.
Max sent EC to FBI HQ on early January debriefing, not mentioning Khallad identification in Kuala Lumpur photographs.
Cole agent e-mailed Max that the source's information was very important to the Cole investigation and discussed interview arrangements.
Max sent EC and FD-302 on the Dec 16, 2000 Khallad identification.
New York Cole case agent and another agent interviewed the source overseas; source again identified Khallad in the Yemeni photograph; CIA case officer present.
Early January 2001 debriefing in which the source identified Khallad in Kuala Lumpur photographs, not communicated to FBI.
Quso reportedly traveled to Bangkok and met Khallad.
CIA and FBI Headquarters discussed status of Cole attack information (fourth missed opportunity regarding Hazmi and Mihdhar).
Hazmi and Mihdhar lived for several months as boarders in the house of an FBI informational asset; the asset mentioned them to control agent Stan, who did not document it.
A joint FBI/CIA source identified Khallad in photographs of the Malaysia meetings; Max was not informed.
New York FBI agents interviewed the joint source without being informed of the Khallad identification.
CIA managers assigned Mary to review CIA cables on the Malaysia meetings and potential Cole connection.
Meeting planned by Donna with Cole investigators, CIA employees and an AUSA to discuss the Cole investigation and Malaysia meetings.
Mary discovered that Hazmi and Mihdhar had traveled to the United States and passed it to the FBI.
Donna learned from Mary that Hazmi and Mihdhar were in the US and sent a routine-precedence EC to New York to open an investigation.

key_claims: The OIG's review covers the FBI's handling of the Phoenix EC, the Moussaoui investigation, and intelligence on Hazmi and Mihdhar before 9/11.
The 'wall' between intelligence and criminal investigations (the 1995 Procedures and the 'primary purpose' standard) is presented as a key background factor.
Hazmi and Mihdhar were identified as al Qaeda operatives in January 2000, following the Malaysia meetings, and later associated with Khallad, the purported Cole mastermind.
Hazmi and Mihdhar had contact in San Diego with Bayoumi and with an FBI asset beginning in May 2000.
The Moussaoui chapter covers the dispute between the Minneapolis FBI and FBI Headquarters over a FISA or criminal search warrant.
The report identifies systemic problems in CIA-FBI information sharing, including the use of detailees at the Counterterrorist Center.
The FBI had at least five opportunities from late 1999 to September 2001 to learn of intelligence about Mihdhar and Hazmi.
The CIA knew Mihdhar held a valid U.S. visa and that Hazmi traveled to the U.S. in January 2000, but the FBI says it was not told until August 2001.
Hazmi and Mihdhar lived in San Diego in 2000, boarding with an FBI source and interacting with a former FBI investigative subject.
Al Qaeda leaders were harbored by the Taliban in Afghanistan from 1996 until 2001.
The Phoenix EC theorized that bin Laden was sending students to U.S. aviation schools, but little action was taken before 9/11.
Al Qaeda leaders were harbored by the Taliban regime in Afghanistan from 1996 until 2001.
Al Qaeda was responsible for 9/11, the USS Cole bombing, and the 1998 East Africa embassy bombings.
Bin Laden came to CIA attention in Sudan 1991-96 and the CIA created a dedicated Bin Laden Unit in 1996.
Before 9/11 the FBI counterterrorism program was considered low priority in the early 1990s and only became a separate division in November 1999.
International terrorism trend shifted toward loosely affiliated Islamic extremists away from state sponsors.
Before 9/11 the FBI Counterterrorism Division was geared toward tactical rather than strategic analysis.
Strategic analysis fell to IRSs housed in a separate Investigative Services Division, and their numbers declined before 9/11.
The wall between intelligence and criminal investigations, built on the 'primary purpose' test, affected both the Moussaoui case and the Hazmi and Mihdhar case.
Because of the wall, criminal investigators were not allowed to join the August 2001 search for Hazmi and Mihdhar.
The Department adopted the 'primary purpose' standard in the 1980s, requiring Criminal Division consultation rather than USAO involvement in intelligence investigations.
Richard Scruggs's 1994 proposal, prompted by the Ames case, was the first to use the term 'wall' for separating criminal and intelligence investigations.
The 1995 Procedures gave OIPR formal oversight over FBI-Criminal Division contacts.
After the 1995 Procedures the FBI dramatically reduced consultations with the Criminal Division, fearing FISA surveillance could be terminated.
A wall inside the FBI between intelligence and criminal investigations developed between 1995 and 1997.
The Minneapolis Moussaoui case needed Criminal Division permission via FBI HQ to approach the USAO for a criminal warrant.
After the 1995 Procedures, the FBI sharply reduced consultation with the Criminal Division because OIPR signaled it could jeopardize FISA coverage.
In late 1999 the FISA Court became the 'wall' for FISA-based al Qaeda cases where intelligence was to be passed to criminal investigators.
The FISA Court learned in 2000-2001 of errors in about 100 FISA applications, mostly involving Terrorist Organization No. 1, including inaccurate descriptions of the wall in New York.
NSA caveats on counterterrorism reporting restricted dissemination to criminal investigators, affecting the Mihdhar information in 2001.
OPR concluded in May 2003 that the FISA errors stemmed from systemic flaws rather than misconduct.
Before 9/11 FBI personnel perceived that seeking prosecutor input could jeopardize FISA warrants, creating a climate of fear.
FISA Court requirements imposed in December 2000 burdened the Cole investigation, requiring IOSs just to track certifications.
The Patriot Act and 2002 Procedures lowered the wall; the FISA Court of Review held the wall was never required by FISA or the Constitution.
Al-Qa'ida was used as a 'foreign power' in FISA applications.
Before 9/11, FISA applications passed through field office, FBI HQ SSA/IOS, NSLU, ITOS management and OIPR before reaching the FISA Court, normally taking months.
Expedited FISAs were reserved for suspected imminent attacks and could be prepared in hours or days.
The FBI acknowledges the Phoenix EC was neither analyzed nor disseminated to other agencies and field offices before 9/11.
Kenneth Williams's EC warned of a coordinated bin Laden effort to place students in US aviation schools.
ACS lead assignment did not notify persons on the attention line, so ECs could go unseen.
Williams' Phoenix EC theorized Bin Laden was sending students to US civil aviation schools, but did not posit planes as missiles.
The EC was marked routine and addressed to RFU/UBLU staff and New York agents but not to any IRSs.
Williams linked Subject No. 1 to Al-Muhjiroun and Ibn Khattab, and Subject No. 2 to Abu Zubaida.
Williams had no prior contact with the UBL Unit, relying on Frank to identify addressees.
The Phoenix EC was routed by ACS to a general ITOS administrative bucket rather than directly to RFU or UBLU, and was assigned to RFU on 30 July 2001.
RFU's Ellen closed the lead on 7 Aug 2001 after informally handing it to UBLU's Jane, without supervisory review.
Jane judged the factual predicate weak, noting that Ibn Khattab and Al-Muhjiroun were not operationally tied to Bin Laden.
The FBI personnel feared the Phoenix EC's recommendations would be seen as racial profiling and would require NSLU review.
Jane sent the EC only informally to Lynn, who found it did not affect her Subject No. 2 work, and no leads were issued.
The OIG found no evidence supporting the former informant's claims that he warned Williams of crop dusters or flight schools in 1996.
The Phoenix EC was a routine theory, not a warning, and did not concern the 9/11 plotters, but it warranted strategic analysis and wider dissemination that it did not receive.
IOSs at FBI HQ could handle and prioritize leads without supervisory input, and the Phoenix EC never reached any supervisor before 9/11.
ACS did not notify all addressees of an EC; only assigned lead holders were notified, so attention-line names often never saw documents.
In New York, the Phoenix EC lead was never assigned to a specific agent and was closed in March 2002; agent Jay judged the theory faulty and left action to HQ.
UBLU was overwhelmed in summer 2001 by al Qaeda threats, Bahrain arrests and USS Cole leads, and no ISD analyst was assigned to it.
Frequent rotation of FBI supervisors left IOSs to manage themselves, and after 9/11 Rolince required ITOS leads be assigned to supervisors.
Pre-9/11 ITOS let IOSs handle and close leads like the Phoenix EC without supervisory input, and leads could be closed without work being done.
The FBI lacked strategic analytical capability on international terrorism; no IRS was assigned to Bin Laden matters in summer 2001.
Operational units could override or block dissemination of analysts' products, as in the NY Field Office blocking an al-Qa'ida attack-planning report.
IRSs were under-resourced, poorly trained and lacked a career path; staffing dropped from 36 hires in 1996 to about 10 by mid-2000.
Information sharing was ad hoc and piecemeal; the Phoenix EC was not disseminated within or outside the FBI before 9/11.
The Phoenix EC contained no imminent-threat warning but warranted wider review and analysis.
The FBI failed to share the Phoenix EC with the Intelligence Community, reflecting ad hoc information sharing.
The FBI's ACS system and ITOS resource shortages impeded dissemination and analysis.
The OIG found no misconduct but errors in judgment by Jane, Ellen, Rob, Lynn and Jay.
FBI conducted little strategic analysis and never connected disparate aircraft/flight school intelligence.
Earlier plots (Manila 1995, Yousef/Murad) included aircraft-as-weapon ideas.
